title: Next roadmap item: provider-neutral task contribution reports
context: The user asked for a clear, production-grade next-release answer to the installed-but-is-it-helping problem and explicitly placed it next on the roadmap. They clarified that Kimi, Codex, Claude, CCC and Watchtower are providers/harnesses: Hunch must remain agnostic.
decision: Make task-scoped contribution evidence the next new roadmap implementation item. Provide one validated report engine and CLI/MCP/typed harness contract, distinguishing exact memory delivery, agent-reported application, independently observed checks and unknowns. A harness can drive lifecycle and deterministic presentation without model compliance. Preserve existing protections, project isolation, private memory boundaries, bounded retention and failure-open reporting. Qualify supported automatic presentation paths and the exact package before release; implementation/test progress does not itself constitute production sign-off.
consequences: Existing live-pilot measurements continue alongside this priority; this does not claim their gates have passed.
The normal experience shows concise evidence and uncertainty without requiring the user to inspect raw tool logs.
No external harness is assumed supported merely because its provider name is mentioned.
alternatives_rejected: Provider- or harness-specific product forks: the user explicitly clarified that Hunch is agnostic.
A tool-call counter or generic agent praise as proof of usefulness: neither establishes a specific contribution and neither answers the original installed-but-is-it-helping question.
Declaring production readiness from unit tests alone: the user requires a production-grade experience, so package, failure-path and real integration evidence remain necessary.
